office.name: Head office (form acknowledgements)
office.note: Roger: flat, unhurried bureaucracy over the desk speaker

ada.name: Ada Venn
ada.note: Lily: velvety British actress, slowed for 68

nessa.name: Nessa Vale
nessa.note: Sarah again, pushed harder: direct and sleepless

lio.name: Lio Vale
lio.note: Jessica: the youngest premade voice, kept literal and steady for a 12-year-old

dalia.name: Dr Dalia Kest
dalia.note: Alice again, slower and heavier: careful vocabulary, moral exhaustion

pavel.name: Pavel Arden
pavel.note: Daniel: formal British, courteous and distracted

june.name: June Calder
june.note: Bella again, brisker and plainer: practical tram driver

anja.name: Anja Reed
anja.note: Laura again, steadier and drier: fast, sceptical electrician

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your name is Ellis Flint. You have worked day security for eleven years. Tonight your predecessor left before you arrived. A pencil lies across the entry ledger. On the last page: DO Not Let The Terminal Keep Your Only Copy. Compare the resident card with the register. Inspect the person, then ask questions. A difference is a reason to investigate, not a verdict. Admit opens the inner door; Deny sends someone into the rain; Quarantine takes them to a containment ward. Hold buys an additional interview but uses one of two staffed holding slots. Nothing advances while you are simply reading.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A visitor last night knew the emergency-contact list by heart. Nobody asked whether she liked any of them.

lines.speaker: marr
lines.text: The scanner is not on your desk yet, and good riddance. My uncle failed it after dental work. Ada knows the building better than the register.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The apartment intercom has been reconnected. It lets you ask another person, not ask the truth. Someone upstairs can be wrong. Someone upstairs can be afraid. At the foot of the shift notes is a list of five names. Four are crossed out. The fifth is yours, but it is written in a hand that looks unpleasantly familiar.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A courier reports a second checkpoint beyond the tram wall. The tram map contains no such stop.

lines.speaker: marr
lines.text: Callers sometimes answer yes before you have asked anything. Ask an open question. We are short of movement permits; genuine residents may carry replacements.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A microfilm reader has arrived with no requisition number. Somebody wanted you to have it. Unlike the terminal, film cannot edit itself. Census corrections are now automatic. Administration says this will reduce uncertainty. The terminal has begun replacing the word missing with returned.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The board has lost a floor. F-wing still draws power, but the census calls it unoccupied.

lines.speaker: marr
lines.text: Heard three bells at the archive. Micah says two are the alarm; the third is a pump. Wrote that down because I keep forgetting which sound is supposed to save us.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At 22:41, the corridor speakers gave the evacuation tone backwards. Every lift opened on a different floor. Whether the breach began at your window or somewhere older is not yet clear. A signal scanner is available. You have two insulated cartridges per shift. Fever, metal and radio equipment can interfere. A low reading is not an acquittal; a high reading is not a sentence.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: An internal audit finds residents who entered before the construction of their apartments. One is listed as a founding tenant.

lines.speaker: marr
lines.text: Use the camera, not your memory of a reflection. The emergency lamp is battery powered. If the grid fails, switch it on; there is no hidden countdown.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Administration has issued a directive: executive authorization supersedes conflicting evidence. No one will put the directive in writing. You can now challenge previous quarantine orders through Communications. A successful appeal releases a living human, but it does not erase the harm already done. The clinic has sent you the names, not the totals.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The census service has scheduled a complete synchronization for 05:17 on the seventh night. No technical description is attached.

lines.speaker: marr
lines.text: An instruction is not evidence. If someone asks you to burn a paper, make a second copy before asking why.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You were hired to classify arrivals. Nobody told you that a classification could be an instruction to become something. The residents have begun making their own records: who cooked, who listened, who came back for somebody else. These records disagree with the official distinction between human and Reproduction. Neither set is a guarantee of kindness.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The containment wing requests family photographs, not blood samples. The old transfer lists suddenly make sense.

lines.speaker: marr
lines.text: If an Echo tells you what it is, listen to the rest of the sentence. Then verify it. Compassion without attention is another kind of negligence.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Seven nights of names are in your ledger. The final synchronization will use every admission, every refusal and every blank file as training for a building that would rather have a perfect population than a living one. Finish the queue. Then decide what leaves Meridian: a warning, a purge order, a new agreement, or a silence the machine cannot fill. The people you protected, and the evidence you actually kept, determine what is possible.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your own file is in the outgoing tray. Under date of return: 17 Oct 1984. Under cause of death: blank.

lines.speaker: marr
lines.text: There is no last instruction. I was waiting for one too.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You keep the outer gate open to a staffed shelter and close the inner census link. The building survives tonight. Behind you, seven days of questions remain unanswered.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At dawn you write every unresolved name by hand. The terminal offers to tidy your notes. You decline. Outside, someone is still waiting, but the waiting is no longer invisible.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Meridian-17 remains inhabited, imperfect and sealed. You protected a boundary. Whether it was the right boundary will be tomorrow’s question.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Administration turns your containment reports into a building-wide sweep. White transport lights move across the ceiling. There are no screams in the summary, because the summary has no field for them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The beds are made with military precision. A bowl of soup cools on a windowsill. Ruth’s ledger records portions for people the census has already subtracted. Keeping everyone out did not keep everyone safe.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The loudspeaker congratulates you on a reduction in uncertainty. For the first time in seven nights you can hear every clock in the checkpoint. Nothing human interrupts them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A knock sounds at the inner door. Then the cupboards. Then the telephone, though nobody is calling. The arrivals no longer need the window. Some wear faces you admitted. Some have been waiting much longer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You guide the people still willing to follow through a service hatch. Behind you the census announces that every resident is accounted for. It is announcing names in your voice.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: From the tram wall Meridian looks warm. Every apartment is occupied. At exactly 05:17 every curtain opens. You keep walking with the book beneath your coat.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Emil disconnects the census speaker and warms the independent transmitter. Your microfilm and carbon numbers become words, and then a signal. Dalia’s authorization is among them. You do not edit it out.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: For twelve seconds the eastern press gives no answer. Then a stranger repeats the names back, including yours. The warning has reached a place the terminal cannot amend.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Meridian’s gates stay shut pending a public inquiry, but the disappeared now have witnesses outside the walls. You have not explained the rain. You have made it harder to use the rain as an excuse.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Orin signs with his own name. Ruth signs as his supervisor. The agreement forbids coercion and impersonation; it does not require a person to lie about their origin to receive shelter.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: There are objections. There should be. You take names, record the risks and establish a right of appeal. Celia’s old phrase becomes a practice rather than a slogan. The first new rule is that nobody vanishes into a category.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At breakfast the oranges are sour. Someone complains. Orin laughs, and nobody agrees what that proves. For once the building permits a question to remain open.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Dalia places the manual key beside Anja’s unaltered wiring diagram. Tomas has locked the lifts clear. Film R-84/17 and Selene’s carbon show that the reference service trains its returns from coerced memories. Your own file bears the first surviving return date. You do not need to solve what you are before deciding what you will do.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Anja’s witnessed diagram identifies A as ventilation, B as alarm and C as census reference. The terminal displays the reverse. There is no timer. Read the paper you protected; choose what you are willing to switch off.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Feeder C falls silent. Ventilation continues. People keep breathing. The returns outside stop answering in chorus. Inside, nobody disappears: the machine copied people; it did not own everything they became. Ada puts a penny under the desk’s short leg. At last, something useful that the record never knew.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The queue is finished. Administration waits for your countersignature. The residents wait for something else. What happens next depends on the people you protected and the evidence you actually kept.

lines.speaker: office
lines.text: Form seventeen B received. Head office thanks you for your diligence.

lines.speaker: office
lines.text: Checklist logged. Head office reminds you that a form is not a decision.

lines.speaker: office
lines.text: Received and filed. The census will reconcile your entries at five seventeen.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your first visitor is waiting at the window. Read what they say beneath the camera view. Every decision tonight begins with looking and listening. Press Next when you are ready.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Beside the desk is head office form 17-B: the eight things you must verify for every visitor. Press Compare on the first row. It lays their card and the register side by side and highlights both facts. Then mark the row Matches or Differs. Agreement is not proof; a difference is a reason to ask.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Two rows need your eyes rather than the register. Open Observe in Papers for their feature and eye colour, and compare their face with the photograph on file on the Terminal. Mark those rows too. Later visitors will not always match their photograph.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Scroll down to the interview and ask the visitor anything. Their answers are recorded. A gentle question and a pressing question open different replies, and you may choose only one approach per visitor. Under Tools, Hold asks the outer desk for an independent paper on them; the intercom, scanner and camera arrive on later nights.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When all eight rows are marked, send form 17-B to head office. Every visitor’s form must be filed before you can sign anything. Head office reads the forms, and so, one day, will the census.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When you have seen enough, sign. Admit opens the inner door. Deny sends her back into the rain. Quarantine sends her to the containment ward. Nothing here decides for you, and every signature asks you to confirm.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The ledger keeps what you signed. Some consequences arrive tonight; others arrive on a later night, when the same person returns. Close the entry to meet the next visitor. From here you are on your own, but the Guide is always in the header.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mara’s return slip has expired. Open the Counterfoil on the terminal: it is the movement desk’s own copy, and it can explain an ordinary mistake.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Open Observe and compare the distinguishing feature with the resident card. Left and right always mean the visitor’s own left and right, as if you were standing in their shoes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Some documents carry a serial number. Compare the return slip’s serial with the counterfoil; two originals cannot share one number.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Call apartment asks someone upstairs whether they expect this visitor. A witness can be tired, frightened or wrong. Their answer joins the interview transcript.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Archive tab holds microfilm and signed originals that the terminal cannot rewrite. Facts you select there can be compared with the card like any other source.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Switch on the battery lamp to see the visitor; there is no countdown. The scanner gives an uncertain reading and uses one of two cartridges per night. Take a still to keep the current face beside the intake photograph.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Comms now lists containment appeals: you can ask the clinic to release someone you quarantined earlier. Administration has begun giving orders without signatures. An order is not evidence.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A visitor who discloses their origin is asking for a different judgement. Listen to the rest of the sentence, then verify it against records of conduct, not species.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A woman taps the glass twice with a folded umbrella. You are not Marr. Good. He never let me finish a sentence. She notices your name strip and stops smiling for half a second.

lines.speaker: ada
lines.text: The memorial garden. Lucet preferred rain to flowers, so I brought neither. There is still a tree out there, although somebody has given it a serial number. Have you been doing nights long, Ellis?

lines.speaker: ada
lines.text: Lives alone; Ruth brings supper. I know a thousand voices, love. Faces are the difficult bit.

lines.speaker: ada
lines.text: I worked the old switchboard. I knew your mother’s extension, and you used to come down after school. You called the little service hatch the night window. Strange name for something you only saw in daylight.

lines.speaker: ada
lines.text: Something you heard yourself. Lucet made terrible paper boats. I put pennies in them to keep them upright. There: a useless memory. A system which only stores useful things would never bother keeping it.

lines.speaker: ada
lines.text: A chair. Not for me, for you. Seven hours is too long to sit as though you are being interrogated.

lines.speaker: ada
lines.text: Then turn that off before you ask me to trust you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ruth is in the kitchen. Ada was visiting the garden. Tell her I saved a bowl, not that I was worried.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The visitor presses a damp hospital pass flat with two shaking fingers. The photograph has been taken after a much better night. It expired while I was still using it.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: Outer clinic, bed twelve. A child stopped breathing every time we moved him. The permit office shut at ten. The child did not consult their hours.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: Flatmate: Leon Voss, separate room. Please ask the questions while I sit. Neither of us needs me falling over.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: Yes. I tried to renew it at 21:40 and again at 22:10. Ward charge signed a paper extension. It should be attached to the permit counterfoil. Please do not make my patients prove they were ill.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: Because we share the flat, unofficially. He has a service apartment he never uses. We are both allowed to have a life the personnel office does not know about.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: I need the insulin in my bag to remain cold. You can search it. Please do not leave it under the desk lamp.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: Then turn that off before you ask me to trust you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ward charge: I signed the extension. Ask her which bed we call the lighthouse. It is twelve. There is no window beside it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A man in a maintenance coat leans into the light. He looks familiar only because the photograph is familiar. Water hangs at his chin without falling.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: Lift four. A hinge failed. The building requires hinges. The resident requires entry. You may record either reason.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: Son: Ivo Rusk. A door is never safe because it is shut. You need to know what the hinges are doing.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: A cable snapped. It cut the right side. My son likes to trace it because it resembles a river. He is a small child. He has always been a small child.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: Seventeen. I meant small relative to the building. People are small relative to the building. There is no contradiction in what I said.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: Uses a borrowed clearance pass when management forgets to renew his own.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: The record says I am necessary. You are not in that field.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Pump foreman: Rusk is asleep in the chair beside me. I can wake him if this is another password exercise.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A teenager presents a pass bearing the stamp of the recreation board. He has obviously practised looking offended. He has not practised being wet.

lines.speaker: ivo
lines.text: The print workshop. We were finishing a safety poster. Big letters. Very safe. You can smell the ink, can’t you?

lines.speaker: ivo
lines.text: Father: Tomas Rusk. Can we agree my father does not need the dramatic version?

lines.speaker: ivo
lines.text: Because it was in the drawer. Look, I missed curfew. I borrowed a pass. I did not borrow somebody’s face. Can you please not write that sentence down?

lines.speaker: ivo
lines.text: A boy called Cal at the east shelter. We were printing handbills for a concert nobody authorized. My father thinks I am fixing a press. He will be angrier about the lie than about Cal.

lines.speaker: ivo
lines.text: Tell my father I was stupid. He knows that already. Do not tell him who I was stupid for.

lines.speaker: ivo
lines.text: Then turn that off before you ask me to trust you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tomas’s recorded message says he is at the pumps. A neighbour confirms Ivo’s room and the broken printing press he uses.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The courier slides a return slip through the tray. It bears the same serial as the voided example pinned beside your ledger. Even the tear crosses the same digit.

lines.speaker: bea
lines.text: The eastern shelter. A delivery to the eastern shelter. A receipt from the eastern shelter. The route contains everything necessary to describe the route.

lines.speaker: bea
lines.text: Sister lives in the eastern shelter. I can bring you a signature or I can bring you what happened. They are not always the same parcel.

lines.speaker: bea
lines.text: It is a common serial. Everybody needs one. A number cannot belong to only one person when so many people require numbers.

lines.speaker: bea
lines.text: Black. One knot. A second knot would delay delivery. Speed is my distinguishing characteristic.

lines.speaker: bea
lines.text: Reuses serialled paper when the depot runs out and lies about carrying letters.

lines.speaker: bea
lines.text: Then turn that off before you ask me to trust you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Depot clerk: Noll has not collected a pass tonight. We are still waiting for her bicycle wheel.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A woman in a kitchen coat places a covered bowl in the tray before her identity card. Documents first, she says in an imitation of somebody else. Soup second. Civilization third.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.text: The supplies shed. I have six onions and an administrative disagreement about whether an onion counts as a whole vegetable. It does if you are hungry enough.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.text: Lives alone; feeds most of floor E. Hungry people are not an accounting error.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.text: Orin Dace, down in F-wing. Quiet fellow. Sometimes he brings things the official garden inventory says do not exist. Those are usually the best things.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.text: He has been cooking with me for five years. That is not an identity test, I know. It is just information about what he has done with five years.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.text: I need you to eat. A person who has not eaten starts seeing enemies because decisions feel like effort.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.text: Then turn that off before you ask me to trust you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Emil answers amid radio hiss. She went for onions. If she brings you soup, eat it before she asks you whether you like it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A man holds a red cup wrapped in cloth. He apologizes for bringing something breakable to a checkpoint. He never apologizes for arriving late.

lines.speaker: pavel
lines.text: The memorial wall. They finally engraved my daughter’s name. They spelled it correctly, which is more than some people get.

lines.speaker: pavel
lines.text: Lives alone; wife and daughter deceased. There are questions people answer wrongly because the answer hurts.

lines.speaker: pavel
lines.text: Six. She put six on it. I know they look like seven, but one is only a mark where the paint ran. Please stop turning it toward the lamp.

lines.speaker: pavel
lines.text: Yes. Seven. There are seven. She made the last one the day before they took her. Sometimes I tell myself she finished the cup earlier than that.

lines.speaker: pavel
lines.text: I need you to understand that remembering is not always something people do willingly.

lines.speaker: pavel
lines.text: Then turn that off before you ask me to trust you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ada: Do not turn sadness into a trick question. He is wrong about the cup when the cup hurts.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A maintenance engineer lays down a permit signed by a supervisor. His cheek bears a thin scar on the left. Someone at the pumps says I came here last night. I did not enjoy hearing that.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: North pumps, then lift four. I slept for two hours in the foreman’s chair. Apparently someone else was using my face while I did it.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: Son: Ivo Rusk. A door is never safe because it is shut. You need to know what the hinges are doing.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: I pinched my writing hand. It is a stupid injury and a legitimate signature. There is an incident slip. Would you prefer I smear blood over your carbon?

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: A wooden bird. I carved it for Ivo when he was six. There is a blue sun underneath the lift now. He thinks I have not noticed.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: Uses a borrowed clearance pass when management forgets to renew his own.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: Then turn that off before you ask me to trust you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ivo: Ask about the wooden bird. He pretends he carved it by accident. My father has never made anything by accident.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The woman outside is greeted by someone behind the inner door. She does not acknowledge the greeting until you finish reading her card.

lines.speaker: celia
lines.text: Distribution shed. Four families were left off the ration list. I brought them back onto the list using the highly irregular technique of writing their names.

lines.speaker: celia
lines.text: Lives with three unnamed evacuees. Keeping people safe has to include keeping them people.

lines.speaker: celia
lines.text: Pell says many things. Three people sleep on my floor because their shelter flooded. I submitted the forms. A form waiting in an office is still a person waiting in the rain.

lines.speaker: celia
lines.text: Keep a chair. Not a seat; a chair can be carried to somebody who cannot reach the table. Ada says I make furniture sound political.

lines.speaker: celia
lines.text: Signs paperwork for people who cannot read and sometimes covers their mistakes.

lines.speaker: celia
lines.text: Then turn that off before you ask me to trust you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nessa: Celia found the shelter list for me. She has not promised me Lio is safe. I trust her more for not promising.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The typist watches the terminal display her birth date. It was the twenty-eighth when I was born. Apparently the office has improved February.

lines.speaker: selene
lines.text: Census annex. I typed forty-six amendments today. I was not allowed to see the originals. My own correction request came back marked amended, which did not make it correct.

lines.speaker: selene
lines.text: Lives alone; cousin: Micah Bell. It is possible for every box to be filled correctly and the form to be a lie.

lines.speaker: selene
lines.text: I know. The clinic register has the real date. My mother was furious about it for years, long before the rain. The replacement card copied the same mistake.

lines.speaker: selene
lines.text: Now they can. A green line arrives from upstairs and the old value disappears. I started keeping carbons. I am telling you that because you still have a pencil.

lines.speaker: selene
lines.text: Do not submit my name as a correction tonight. It might attract the kind of attention that corrects the person instead.

lines.speaker: selene
lines.text: Then turn that off before you ask me to trust you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Micah: My cousin has always hated her birthday because the bureaucracy adds imaginary days to it. She is not new.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A man with round spectacles taps the microphone grille as though testing a transmitter. His smile appears a moment after the tapping stops.

lines.speaker: emil
lines.text: The scrap depot. I repaired a radio for my sister Ruth. She lives with me. A family is a group of residents sharing a registered number.

lines.speaker: emil
lines.text: Neighbour and emergency contact: Ruth Sable. A noise is a message only after somebody agrees what to listen for.

lines.speaker: emil
lines.text: Neighbour is an old word. Sister is a closer word. Closer relationships improve residential stability. Surely you prefer the closer word.

lines.speaker: emil
lines.text: My wife has never existed. I have no use for an additional relationship. Why are you asking for a relationship the record does not require?

lines.speaker: emil
lines.text: Collects stolen wire and sees conspiracies in ordinary clerical mistakes.

lines.speaker: emil
lines.text: Then turn that off before you ask me to trust you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ruth: My brother? I have no brother. Emil is soldering at the kitchen table. Shall I tell him he has acquired a sister?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A woman hands you an old evacuation card from grid G-999. On its back she has written the word Lio until there is almost no paper left.

lines.speaker: nessa
lines.text: Every shelter the tram still reaches. I found a shoe that was not his. That is the best news I have had all evening.

lines.speaker: nessa
lines.text: Child: Lio Vale; partner deceased. You can mark me difficult after you tell me whether you saw my child.

lines.speaker: nessa
lines.text: It is an evacuation grid, from before C-wing was finished. I lost the new card climbing the shelter fence. Ask the laundry crew. Ask Mara. Ask anyone who has seen me keep going.

lines.speaker: nessa
lines.text: Ask what he calls his toy tram. Window. And when he is scared he calls me Ness. People think Little Lion is sweet. He hates it.

lines.speaker: nessa
lines.text: Goes outside without authorization to search shelters; conceals that from officials.

lines.speaker: nessa
lines.text: Then turn that off before you ask me to trust you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mara: I treated her hands this afternoon. She went over a fence looking for Lio. Her old card is real.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A child stands below the bottom edge of the interview light. An unfamiliar initial has been added to his identity card. He keeps looking toward the tram lane.

lines.speaker: lio
lines.text: The west shelter. A driver gave me a coat. I got on the wrong tram and then I was embarrassed to say I was lost. It got too dark to be embarrassed after that.

lines.speaker: lio
lines.text: Mother: Nessa Vale. The room on the map has a door. The room in the building does not.

lines.speaker: lio
lines.text: They wrote E because I came from the eastern queue. It is not my name. My name is on the school sheet. Can you call Ness?

lines.speaker: lio
lines.text: My tram. Not this window. The little one. One wheel comes off if you turn too hard, so you have to drive slowly even when you are late.

lines.speaker: lio
lines.text: I need someone to tell me whether I am in trouble before I tell them everything.

lines.speaker: lio
lines.text: Then turn that off before you ask me to trust you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nessa’s line is engaged. June confirms the child, the coat and the toy with a loose wheel. She refuses to guess whether Nessa is already home.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The mortuary attendant removes his hat. The lamp casts its brim across the wall. Below it, the shape of the man leaves the floor strangely uninterrupted.

lines.speaker: hadi
lines.text: The transfer wing. I have returned six occupied units to the disposal record. No relatives are required. Relatives complicate completion.

lines.speaker: hadi
lines.text: Lives alone; helps Pavel after memorial visits. The living deserve uncertainty. The dead deserve their names.

lines.speaker: hadi
lines.text: It is a maintenance issue. Report it after admitting me. I have a delivery inside and the delivery cannot wait for optics.

lines.speaker: hadi
lines.text: Disposal. It is the authorized term. Return would imply that the recipient matters.

lines.speaker: hadi
lines.text: Works with chemical residues and sometimes carries identity tags belonging to dead people.

lines.speaker: hadi
lines.text: Then turn that off before you ask me to trust you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Leon: Morrow says return, even when I tell him that is not the form heading. Hold him at the lamp while I check the mortuary.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The archivist sets a film canister beside his card. It is not for the projector. It is for you to keep after the projector tells you it never existed.

lines.speaker: micah
lines.text: The archive annex. They called a flood drill in a room without pipes and ordered everyone away from the film cabinets. I went in the other direction.

lines.speaker: micah
